thesis: Update on the open position from 2026-10-09 at 17.1, last 14.63, -14.4% and only 0.23 above its 14.4 stop - 0.20 of a 1.161 ATR. AstraZeneca agreed on 2026-09-28 to buy $2.0B of convertible preferred at an implied 18.3561 per common share, so a strategic buyer paid 25% above where the stock now trades, but conversion of the 108,955,369 underlying shares is blocked until shareholders double the authorised common, and that supply overhang is what has driven the stock down 14.6% in four sessions. Levels are unchanged and the honest win probability is below the break-even baseline.
key_risk: The stop is 0.23 away against a 1.161 ATR that is 7.94% of price, so a gap straight through 14.4 is an ordinary day rather than a tail. Beyond that: the proxy doubles authorised shares to 2.0B to cover the conversion plus an at-the-market programme, which is dilution with no date on it, and if the authorised-share increase is not effective within 18 months of issuance Summit must redeem the $2.0B preferred for cash at a price tied to market value - a cash call a clinical-stage company cannot fund from operations. The clinical collaboration announced alongside the placement disclosed no trial design, timing or data. Conviction is 3 and this is a 1% speculative line, not a position to defend.
counter_argument: The bull case is the 25% discount to what AstraZeneca paid three weeks ago, which is as strong a third-party valuation mark as this kind of asset gets, and $2.0B of gross proceeds removes financing risk for years. It is not enough to hold the trade: the discount exists precisely because 109M conversion shares and an ATM sit between here and that mark, the vote that unlocks them has a placeholder date, and the position sits a fifth of an ATR above its stop. Being right about the asset and wrong about the supply is how this loses, so the stop stands and the re-entry is deferred until the vote is dated and passed.

thesis: Comcast has reported 1.04, 0.79, 0.84 and 1.12 over its last four quarters, so trailing EPS is 3.79 against a 21.90 price - 5.78x earnings on a $77.7B market cap, with three beats in those four quarters and analyst revisions improving. The claim is a multiple claim, not a growth claim: at 7.5x trailing the shares are worth 28.40, which is independently where the 120-day high of 28.31 sits, so the valuation anchor and the price history agree on roughly the same number. The entry is deliberately set below the 120-day low because the one thing wrong with the idea is that nothing has stopped falling yet.
key_risk: The core business is in structural decline and a low multiple on a shrinking earnings base is not cheap, it is correctly priced - the trap in every cable value thesis. Management is not buying either: zero open-market insider purchases in six months, and zero insider sales too, so there is no insider signal in either direction at a stock trading at 5.8x. This lane is also the report's worst: long_term is 0 for 4 on hitting target with an average of -15.2%, which argues for a higher bar rather than a bigger position, hence 2% and a staged entry. INVALIDATION, which replaces a stop: trailing four-quarter EPS falling below 3.20, or EPS missing consensus in two consecutive quarters. Either would mean the earnings base is eroding faster than the multiple can recover, and the thesis is then wrong regardless of price.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is momentum, and it is unanimous: CMCSA lags SPY on every window measured, -4.41% over one month, -7.91% over three and -26.09% over six against SPY +0.09%, +2.85% and +7.48%, and it lags its own sector proxy XLC by 2.60, 7.48 and 18.72 points over the same windows. Buying that is catching something falling relative to everything around it. This is not answered away, it is answered structurally: the entry is placed under 20.50, below the 120-day low, so the idea only ever starts if the decline first reaches a level, and it is staged in thirds down to 19.00 rather than committed at once. What the valuation work does answer is whether the fall has gone far enough to matter - at 5.78x trailing against a 4.5x bear case the downside is 22% while the 7.5x re-rating is 30% up from the entry, and the business beat consensus in three of the last four quarters while the multiple was compressing, which is the gap between the earnings and the price that the trade is buying.
